cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Colossae. He just told them the Father rescued them from the dominion of darkness and brought them into the kingdom of His beloved Son. Now Paul's going to tell them who that Son is, and friend, he's about to gush like a new dad scrolling his phone for pictures.

cards.question: God is invisible. Paul says the Son is the ___ of the invisible God.

cards.text: Then Paul calls Him the firstborn over all creation. And Paul doesn't leave us scratching our hats, because the very next line tells why.

cards.question: Paul calls the Son the firstborn over all creation. Why does he say that?

answers.text: Because all things were created in Him
Because He was the first to walk the earth
Because He was the first to serve God

cards.text: And Paul means ALL things, not some, not most: things in heaven and on earth, even thrones, dominions, rulers and authorities.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says only the things people can see were created through the Son.
All things were created through the Son. Who does Paul say they were created for?
Paul says the Son is before all things. True or false: Paul also says all things hold together in Him.

cards.text: The WHOLE universe holds together in Him, and I can't hold ONE cookie box with my mustache without sprinkles going everywhere. Now Paul turns to the church, and he pictures it as a body.

cards.question: Paul pictures the church as a body. He says the Son is the ___ of the body.

cards.text: He's also the beginning, the firstborn from among the dead. Firstborn over creation, firstborn from the dead, head of the church, and I'm over here bragging that my edges came back SHARP!

cards.question: Paul says the Son is the beginning and the firstborn from among the dead. What's it all for?

answers.text: So He has first place in all things
So the church grows in number
So the rulers bow before Him

cards.question: Paul says something pleased God about the Son. True or false: God was pleased to have only part of His fullness dwell in Him.

cards.text: And God was pleased, through the Son, to reconcile all things to Himself, things on earth and things in heaven. Baker, I couldn't even reconcile the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, and all THEY argued about was who had more charge left!

cards.question: God reconciles all things to Himself through the Son. How is that peace made?

answers.text: Through the blood of His cross
Through the law given at Sinai

cards.text: Now Paul makes it personal and tells the Colossians, "Once you were alienated from God and were hostile in your minds, engaging in evil deeds." Friend, that's a darker place than the back of any junk drawer, and trust me, I'd know.

cards.question: That's who the Colossians were once. But now they've been reconciled. How?

answers.text: By Christ's physical body through death
By keeping every part of the law
By the offerings they brought to God

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the Colossians were reconciled to be presented holy, unblemished and blameless in His presence.
Paul adds an if for the Colossians. All this holds if they continue in their ___.

cards.text: Paul tells them to stay established and firm, not moved from the hope of the gospel, which has been proclaimed to every creature under heaven. And after ALL those big titles for the Son, Paul's own title is one word, as he says, "of which I, Paul, have become a servant."

findings.problem: The card uses facts from outside 1:13 but cites only 1:13. 'The believers in Colossae' comes from Col 1:2, and 'the Father' is named in Col 1:12, since the 'He' of 1:13 points back to the Father in 1:12.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Col 1:13 says the Father 'has rescued us.' Paul counts himself in. The card says the Father rescued 'them,' which leaves Paul out.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story card says 'Paul means ALL things, not some, not most.' Card 6 then asks whether only the things people can see were created through the Son. The setup line rules out the True answer before the baker gets to choose.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'The WHOLE universe holds together in Him' renames what Col 1:17 calls 'all things.' The passage includes things in heaven and invisible things, not just 'the universe.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke 'my edges came back SHARP' is a callback to his renewal out of the drawer. That setup hasn't come up in this lesson, and only the junk drawer itself is known from onboarding. A baker may not know his edges were ever worn down.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'So the rulers bow before Him' comes close to the right answer, 'So He has first place in all things.' Rulers bowing to Him is one way of Him having first place, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke's action is settling an argument between other parties (the batteries arguing with each other). Col 1:20 is God reconciling all things to Himself. The comparison doesn't share the same core action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Cards 9, 11 and 14 all use the same joke template: the Son does something huge, and Papa Dorin can't even manage a small version of it (hold a cookie box, brag about sharp edges, reconcile the batteries). The humor runs on a repeated formula instead of fitting each moment.

rule.text: No formula. His personality fits whatever moment he's in, whether it's a tense moment in a story, a hard teaching or a quick question. There are no joke quotas and no required kinds of jokes.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'That's who the Colossians were once,' which points back to card 16. Card 16 is no longer on screen, so the question doesn't say what 'that' is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Card 17's wrong answers ('keeping every part of the law' and 'the offerings they brought to God') repeat the wrong answers card 15 just ruled out ('the law given at Sinai' and 'offerings at the temple'). The question is about a new verse, but the baker can get it right just by remembering card 15's answers.
findings.question: Can a later choice card reuse wrong answers that an earlier card has already shown are wrong, or does that count as giving the answer away? The rules allow an easy follow-up, but they don't address reusing wrong answers.

findings.problem: 'All this holds if they continue in their ___' has two problems. First, 'All this' points back to cards the baker can't see. Second, it says the whole reconciliation depends on the condition. In Col 1:22-23, the 'if' is attached to being presented holy, unblemished and blameless, and the text doesn't spell out how far the condition reaches.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Paul tells them to stay established and firm' turns the condition in Col 1:23 ('if indeed you continue in your faith, established and firm, not moved...') into a command. The text gives a condition, not an instruction.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
